findings.title: Cache is set before the limit check, so a rejected device is allowed on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate fails once, but the key stays cached for 29 minutes. The next request for that device hits the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and anonymous authentication succeeds without ever recording the device. The configurable limit is therefore bypassed by any client that retries within the cache TTL. Set the cache only after a successful write, and do not treat a cached rejection as success.

findings.title: Device limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts recent devices and, if the count is under AnonymousDeviceLimit, inserts in a separate session with no transaction or row lock. Concurrent first-time devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, so the stored device count exceeds the configured cap and anonymous auth is granted past the limit. The count and the insert/upsert need to be serialized (single transaction with a lock, or an insert that fails when the cap is already reached).

findings.title: Wire providers changed but generated injectors are not updated
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer takes anonstore.AnonStore and now takes db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit argument. Grafana builds this graph with Google Wire and commits wire_gen.go; this PR does not update wire.go or wire_gen.go. Wire cannot provide a bare int64 to ProvideAnonDBStore, so regeneration will fail and the current generated injector will not compile against the new signatures.

findings.title: device_limit is not added to defaults.ini
findings.body: auth.anonymous device_limit is read via MustInt64(0) (0 means unlimited) but conf/defaults.ini and sample config are unchanged. Operators have no documented key, default, or meaning, and Grafana config docs are generated from defaults.ini, so the new limit cannot be discovered or set from the shipped configuration.
